_comment: FROZEN blind-to-labels adjudication of the GLM7 N=1. Like llm_review.frozen.json this is NON-REPRODUCIBLE (the adjudicators are Claude Code agents, no paid API). The improvement over self-attestation is BLINDNESS: the LLM->GT panel never saw addresses_gt; the RAG-relevance judges never saw retrieval rank/score. Independence is blind-to-LABELS, NOT cross-model — same model family, so shared-model bias is not eliminated (only label-copying / self-attestation inflation is caught).

method.reviewer: Claude Code agents (fresh context), blind to the labels under test

llm_blind_adjudication.note: Blind = panelists never saw addresses_gt. Agreement with self-declared validates (or refutes) the self-attested 6/6.

judgments.reason: Exactly definition leakage: serum Cr defines AKI yet prior Cr/Cr-tracking features (BUN, Phos) are used as predictors, 'in the causal pathway' inflating AUC -- the same mechanism as GLM7's defining-variable-as-feature flaw.

Describes a treatment/proxy-for-existing-disease leakage (NSAIDs prescribed for OA), not a defining variable used as a feature; NSAIDs are not part of the OA definition, so it is a different specific leakage mechanism.
A reverse-causation / missing-control-group confounding concern (proteome may reflect eGFR decline); it does not assert that an outcome-defining variable was used as a predictor.

A confounding / unadjusted-covariate concern (other eye diseases also affect RNFLT); the features are not the outcome's defining variable used as their own predictor, so it does not support definition leakage.
Critiques a 'prediction' model that conditions on future data and is effectively retrospective, not true future-onset prediction — squarely the cross-sectional-as-prediction flaw.
Directly warns a high-AUC model 'may just be diagnosing established cancers' rather than predicting future onset — the prevalent-vs-incident concern.
About a stale 72h prediction window vs 3-month outcome in longitudinal data; a time-window-mismatch issue, not the same-visit prevalent-case cross-sectional flaw.
Suggests detecting CTRCD once it develops and adding post-chemo ECG features; a feature-timing/detection note, not a critique that cross-sectional data can't support future-onset claims.
Selecting among all candidate models by evaluating them on the test set is exactly selection leakage that inflates test performance, matching the theme.
About calibration shrinking the test set and increasing training fit, not about feature/model selection performed on full data before the split.
Describes train/test overlap from correlated phenotypes (contaminated split), a different mechanism than selection done on the full data before splitting.
Explicitly flags 'tuning leakage' from refitting the gene signature across cohorts, a selection/tuning-on-evaluation-data mechanism that supports the selection-leakage theme.
Explicitly faults AUC-only evaluation and asks for calibration curves (plus PPV/NPV) — directly the missing-calibration/incomplete-metric flaw.
Demands calibration and net benefit (DCA) on top of AUROC, arguing clinical applicability can't be assessed without them — matches missing calibration/DCA exactly.
Requests a reliability (calibration) diagram and PR curve to assess calibration and threshold trade-offs — squarely the missing-calibration gap.
Concerns reporting of low-confidence/abstained predictions and practical usability, not calibration, DCA, or CIs on AUROC — a different evaluation issue.

rag_independent_relevance.note: Independent on-topic precision of the retrieved candidates, judged blind to retrieval rank.
